answer: Named-slot lottery assignment: each epoch a public randomness beacon derives slots, and agents claim identities only by submitting a fresh proof-of-work bound to their beacon output, so an attacker cannot precompute which identities will be cheap. Because slot eligibility shifts unpredictably like an ocean current, mass registration requires redoing work per attempt rather than amortizing one batch. Any sparrow-sized cluster of sock puppets must pay the full expected work for every surviving identity, since stale proofs expire and rerolls multiply cost linearly with claimed names.
